title: cross-team-rollout-persona-matrix-and-safety-script-wip
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working doc to align cross-functional partners on who does what during very small-batch rollouts (micro-releases), safety checks for canaries and A/B slices, and a compact communication + escalation script.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: rolling new LLM routing logic, model-variant swaps, and latency-optimized quantization profiles.
- NOT covered here: infra capacity procurement, billing/legal approvals (assume those are pre-cleared).
- Target audience: product owners, release stewards, SRE/oncall, applied ML, UX, and CS owners.
- Tone: operational checklist + persona matrix + short comms templates (intended for on-call and stewards).

Quick summary (one-liner):
A 6-step microrelease flow + persona matrix that codifies signal ownership, fast rollback triggers, and a standard one-paragraph comms script to reduce hesitation during triage.

Persona matrix (who does what)
- Release Steward (RS) [Product/PM]: single throat to choke for activation, approves exposure, calls snapshot.
- Experiment Owner (EO) [Applied ML/Product]: defines evals, hypothesis, sampling method, expected QoQ metrics, and approves measurement hooks.
- SRE/Oncall (SRE): watches infra/latency/error budgets, executes traffic routing changes and rollbacks, owns runbook automation.
- Observability Lead (OBS) [Console team]: configures dashboards and alert thresholds, runs live drift checks for model outputs (e.g., hallucination signals, toxicity heuristics).
- Customer Success (CS): triage customer tickets for affected orgs, prepped to send external comms if SLA impacted.
- Legal/Privacy (LP): available as a consult for data-retention/PII concerns during canary if enabled.

Steward responsibilities (condensed)
- Before activation: confirm smoke test pass, slice selection, fallback mapping, and cost guardrails.
- At activation: announce on #rollouts channel, start timer for first-observation window (default 15m), maintain decision log.
- During: keep heartbeat updates every 15 minutes in the event channel until stable.
- On anomaly: if any hard trigger fires, call an immediate rollback and notify the oncall SRE.
- Post: run release retrospective within 3 business days, capture telemetry and lessons.

Signal catalog (operational triggers)
- Hard triggers (immediate rollback):
  - 5xx error rate > 1% absolute in the canary slice sustained for 5m.
  - p95 latency increase > 300ms absolute or >50% relative vs baseline for 3 consecutive windows.
  - Crashloop or model OOM on dedicated host.
  - Safety classifier spike (toxicity/hallucination) above agreed threshold (see EO signal table).
- Soft triggers (investigate / pause exposure):
  - Significant drop in relevance/CTR (endpoint-specific) beyond expected variance.
  - Cost per token spike beyond threshold for reserved capacity customers.
  - Elevated user complaints or CS tickets referencing degraded quality.

Telemetry & dashboards (minimum)
- Per-slice p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, tail-kernel failures.
- Model quality probes: semantic-similarity drift vs control, hallucination classifier rate, stop-word/length anomalies.
- Token- and inference-cost counters (per-model, per-slice).
- Signal retention: keep 1 week high-cardinality traces, 90 days aggregated. (Confirm with LP before longer retention.)

Canary sizing guidance (heuristic)
- Very small microrelease: 0.5% traffic or 1000 requests (whichever is larger) for first 1–2 hours.
- If safety/quality sensitive: start at 0.1% with synthetic traffic probing first.
- For A/B experiments: ensure sample size supports primary metric; quick heuristic: for a categorical quality signal with baseline ~5%, need ~N per arm ~10k to detect ~1% absolute change (high-level; EO to compute precise sample sizes).

A/B test quick-checklist (pre-activation)
- Hypothesis written and ownership assigned.
- Primary/secondary metrics defined + alert thresholds.
- Randomization stratified by region and customer tier to avoid confounding.
- Data collection hooks validated (IDs, hashing, TTL).
- Analysis notebook stub created and linked.

Activation ceremony (15-point checklist)
1. RS confirms stakeholder roster and incident channel created.
2. EO confirms eval harness passed on canary seed set.
3. SRE validated routing config + fallback mapping preloaded.
4. OBS verified dashboard and alert rules deployed.
5. CS notified of the slice and standby window.
6. Smoke test executed against slice with known inputs.
7. Start timer + open decision log.
8. Gradual exposure ramp plan set (0.1 → 0.5 → 1.0% typical).
9. Token cost guardrail thresholds set.
10. Canary synthetic probe started (if applicable).
11. Paging/alert thresholds confirmed and owners pinned.
12. Rehearsed rollback command and owner ready.
13. Communications template prepped.
14. Observability-led first-pass checklist complete.
15. RS flips activation flag.

Communication & escalation script (copy-paste)
- Initial announcement (on #rollouts and emailed to stakeholders):
  "Activating microrelease: [brief description], slice: [slice], exposure: [x%], RS: [name], EO: [name], SRE-oncall: [name]. Watchlist window: T+0-120m. If p95 latency > X or 5xx > Y or safety classifier > Z, rollback immediately and tag RS."
- Incident escalation template (if anomaly):
  "ANOMALY: [metric] breached at [time]. Impact: [customer-visible / infra-only]. Action: SRE to rollback; RS to notify stakeholders; EO to gather sample IDs and earliest failing traces."

Rollback decision matrix (fast):
- If any hard trigger: SRE executes rollback, announces in channel, RS confirms.
- If soft triggers and ambiguous: pause ramp, collect another data window (30m), EO performs quick sample audit. If unresolved, escalate to on-call lead.

Post-mortem and dataset capture (must-haves)
- Capture: request ids, raw model outputs (10–50k samples depending on privacy), metric deltas, recent config commits, routing table snapshot.
- EO to run focused evaluation harness and determine whether model/regression caused issue or traffic artifact.
- Timeline and decision log posted to Confluence; include remediation and change to rollout rules if needed.

Open questions / TODOs (short list)
- Agree on a single canonical safety classifier and thresholds across teams (EO + OBS + Safety).
- Decide synthetic probe cadence and template per model family.
- Automate heartbeat messages into channel (ops automation).
- Formalize sample size calculator into a small web tool (EO + DX).

Notes to self (work-in-progress tone)
- Keep this doc compact — the aim is a one-pager for stewards with links to deep-dive docs.
- Next step: sync with SRE on causal-chain playbook for noisy network events vs model regressions.
- Ping legal for retention constraints before recommending 30k sample captures.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: rollout playbook (linked in metadata)
- Github: rollout-scripts repo (linked)
- Jira: ROLL board (linked)

End of doc — callout: this is intentionally terse and opinionated; please edit in place and flag anything that would block a 15-minute canary activation.
